steps.body: Sides known, angle missing — run the ratio BACKWARD. If sin θ = 0.5, then θ = sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30°: the inverse function asks “which angle has this sine?” One notation warning: **sin⁻¹ is NOT 1/sin** — the −1 marks an inverse function, not a reciprocal.

widget.prompt: sin θ = 0.5. Drag the angle until the opp/hyp card reads 0.5 — that is what an inverse sine does.
widget.successFeedback: θ = 30°. Finding an angle from a ratio is the same table read backwards, which is all sin⁻¹ means: not a new operation, but the question 'which angle gives this ratio?'.
widget.lowFeedback: opp/hyp is still below 0.5 — open the angle further.
widget.highFeedback: opp/hyp has gone past 0.5 — close the angle a little.
widget.scaleFeedback: Resize the triangle before checking; the angle that gives 0.5 must not depend on the triangle's size.

explanationVariants: Rise over run is tangent's pair: θ = tan⁻¹(3/4) = tan⁻¹(0.75) ≈ 36.9°.
The two LEGS are known — no hypotenuse needed, so tangent's inverse fires.

widget.prompt: A ramp rises 3 ft over a 4 ft run. What angle does it make with the ground, in degrees? (Round to tenths.)

commonErrors.feedback: 53.1° is tan⁻¹(4/3) — the ratio flipped, giving the OTHER acute angle. Rise over run: tan⁻¹(0.75) ≈ 36.9°.
0.75 is the ratio itself — the last step is missing. Feed it to the inverse: tan⁻¹(0.75) ≈ 36.9°.

steps.body: Which inverse? Same matching game as before: identify WHICH two sides you hold, and take that ratio's inverse. Opposite-and-hypotenuse → sin⁻¹. Adjacent-and-hypotenuse → cos⁻¹. The two legs → tan⁻¹. The sides choose the function for you.

widget.prompt: You know the opposite side (6) and the hypotenuse (12). The angle is:

options.label: sin⁻¹(6/12) = 30°
options.feedback: Right — opposite with hypotenuse is sine's pair, so its inverse recovers the angle.

options.label: cos⁻¹(6/12) = 60°
options.feedback: Cosine pairs the ADJACENT with the hypotenuse — but 6 is the opposite side. That computes a different angle.

options.label: tan⁻¹(6/12) ≈ 26.6°
options.feedback: Tangent needs the two LEGS — and 12 is the hypotenuse, not a leg. Sine's pair is what you actually hold.

options.label: sin(0.5)
options.feedback: That FEEDS 0.5 to sine instead of inverting — sine eats angles and outputs ratios. Recovering the angle needs sin⁻¹.

explanationVariants: The 13 ft ladder is the hypotenuse and the 12 ft height is opposite the ground angle: θ = sin⁻¹(12/13) ≈ 67.4°.
Steep is right — the ladder reaches nearly its full length up the wall.

widget.prompt: A 13 ft ladder reaches 12 ft up a wall. What angle does it make with the GROUND, in degrees? (Round to tenths.)

commonErrors.feedback: 22.6° is cos⁻¹(12/13) — the angle at the TOP of the ladder, against the wall. The ground angle has the 12 ft height as its opposite: sin⁻¹(12/13) ≈ 67.4°.
0.92 is the ratio 12/13 itself — the inverse hasn't run yet. sin⁻¹(12/13) ≈ 67.4°.

steps.body: Built-in check: a right triangle's two acute angles always total 90°. Find one with an inverse and the other is 90° minus it — 36.9° pairs with 53.1°. If your two inverses don't add to 90°, a ratio got flipped somewhere.

widget.prompt: One acute angle of a right triangle is 36.9°. What is the other, in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 143.1 is 180 − 36.9 — but the right angle already claims 90° of the triangle's 180°. The acute pair shares what's left: 90 − 36.9 = 53.1°.
Equal acute angles only happen in the 45-45-90 triangle. Here the pair must total 90°: 90 − 36.9 = 53.1°.

explanationVariants: Drop and horizontal run are the two legs: θ = tan⁻¹(25/60) ≈ 22.6° below horizontal.
No hypotenuse is given — tangent's inverse is the only ratio whose two sides you hold.

widget.prompt: A zipline drops 25 m over a 60 m horizontal run. What angle does it make below the horizontal, in degrees? (Round to tenths.)

commonErrors.feedback: 67.4° is tan⁻¹(60/25) — the ratio flipped. The DROP is the opposite side of the pitch angle: tan⁻¹(25/60) ≈ 22.6°.
24.6° is sin⁻¹(25/60) — but 60 m is the horizontal RUN, a leg, not the cable's slanted length. Two legs ⇒ tangent: ≈ 22.6°.

hints: Which two sides do you hold — and is either one the hypotenuse?
Drop (opposite) and run (adjacent) are both legs: tangent's pair.

takeaways: Inverse trig recovers the angle from a ratio — and sin⁻¹ is an inverse, not a reciprocal.
Match the two KNOWN sides to their ratio, then invert that one.
The two acute inverses must total 90° — a free error check.
steps.teaser: Next: a new way to measure angles entirely — the radian — built from the circle itself.

concept.body: The friendliest inverse: tan θ = 1 means the opposite and adjacent are EQUAL — rise matches run — and the only acute angle that balanced is 45°. So tan⁻¹(1) = 45°. Every inverse question reads the same way: which angle produces this ratio?

explanationVariants: tan⁻¹(1) = 45° — equal legs make the half-square triangle.
The inverse outputs an ANGLE, not another ratio.

widget.prompt: tan θ = 1. Find θ in degrees.

commonErrors.feedback: 1 is the ratio, not the angle — the inverse still has to run: tan⁻¹(1) = 45°.
tan 90° is undefined (the adjacent side collapses to 0). Equal legs happen at 45°.
